headline: Trust, Tests and the E-Rate Line
thesis: New survey data show students rewriting their work to dodge AI detectors while faculty confidence erodes, as K-12 leaders rally to defend E-Rate and harden recovery plans.
summary: Tuesday's digest centers on a trust gap around AI. An Inside Higher Ed Student Voice survey of 5,034 undergraduates finds eight in ten use generative or agentic AI routinely and a quarter have changed how they write to avoid false AI-detector flags, while 88% of surveyed faculty say AI has hurt their confidence in the authenticity of student work. On the K-12 side, CoSN delivered a petition from 464 leaders in 35 states urging Congress to protect E-Rate as the FCC reviews the program, and EdTech Magazine explains how isolated recovery environments help districts bounce back from ransomware. 1EdTech's new AI-evaluation white paper and EdTech Digest's "evidence season" column keep efficacy in focus, and the fall conference circuit (OLC Accelerate, CITE, BrainStorm) is in full swing.
footnote: Compiled from 11 curated edtech sources · NOVEMBER 17, 2026 · Items were gathered via web search; ISTE, Brookings, EdTech Week, Ed-Fi and Education Technology Insights had no new dated items, so evergreen pieces are shown.
